stages.text: Official accident theory — incomplete, not yet disproven.

The Silent Lion appears to predate the modern Gryffindor emblem. Surviving depictions emphasize observation and restraint rather than strength or aggression.

Interpretation: it may represent restraint, patience, or duty without recognition — unconfirmed.
Peeves knows a rhyme connected to the Silent Lion: "Lion waits and eagle sees. Badger keeps and serpent weighs. Four may knock but one may walk. Ask the man who never talks."
Professor Binns claims to have seen Ashcombe near the collapsed corridor before his death.
Binns never saw a face or heard a voice — only a dark academic cloak. Downgraded from identification to possible sighting.
A page is missing from Ashcombe's notebook.
The recovered page references an unknown mechanism beneath the collapsed corridor. The eagle fragment matches part of the drawing.
Benedict Hale and Elias Ashcombe were longtime friends.
Benedict claims he last spoke with Ashcombe several weeks before the accident. Follow-up recommended.
